newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU oil stock data surprise few, deemed neutral.
newsitem.headline: EU oil stock data surprise few, deemed neutral.

text.p: Figures for April oil stocks in the European Union were largely in line with seasonal norms and were broadly neutral, analysts said on Tuesday.
"They're not bullish, but they also don't support your case if you're a devout bear," said Geoff Pyne, oil analyst at bank UBS.
Crude and oil product stocks combined rose by 2.11 million barrels, or 0.2 percent, to 1,083.55 million barrels at the end of April. The build was the result of a large increase in crude oil stocks.
Crude stocks were up 13.00 million barrels, or 3.1 percent, to 427.42 million barrels, as stocks in France and the Netherlands grew. In each country, inventories rose by 5.8 million tonnes.
However, year-on-year, overall European crude stocks were barely changed.
"It was a fairly big crude build but that's the sort of thing we would expect," said Pyne.
The only element of surprise, for some, was that the crude build came at the same time as an increase in refinery runs.
Crude intake was 660,000 barrels per day (bpd), or 5.8 percent, higher than in March at 11.957 million bpd.
Stocks of all the major products over the same period fell.
Middle distillate stocks were down the most, falling by 6.60 million barrels, or 2.1 percent, to 311.48 million barrels, the greatest fall being in Italy.
That left them 11.89 million barrels, or 4.0 percent, higher than a year ago.
For some this represented a tightening of the market.
"The year-on-year surplus is down dramatically," said Mike Barry of oil consultants Energy Market Consultants.
At the end of March, the yearly distillate surplus was over 30 million barrels.

Some analysts, however, maintained their bearish line on distillates, mentioning that the draw was the result of large-scale demand from the Asia-Pacific region and not due to any improvement in the European market.

"The (refinery) turnaround in the Asia-Pacific should be winding down in June, so we'll see a sharp tale-off. Gas oil is definitely still bearish. The figures are still way above historical levels," said Cindy Poynter of oil consultants Bonner and Moore.

Gasoline inventories dropped by 5.35 million barrels, or 3.1 percent, in April to 168.73 million barrels and were 1.70 million barrels, or 1.0 percent, lower than a year ago. As with middle distillates, the greatest month-on-month fall was in Italy.

The draw was slightly under most estimates and the year-on-year shortfall has narrowed. However, the figures did not alter the reasonably healthy state of the market in Europe, albeit a market reliant on continuing demand from the United States, analysts said.
